Fetch the Mayor from the Town Hall (HaHaland)
Take the Mayor to Mother Nox's table
column2: Lleva al Alcalde a la mesa de Madre Nox

column1: I'm scared of the dark.
I miss my brother.
I never liked grape.
I'm tired all the time.
I broke the vase. In 1999.
I don't know how to swim.
I cry at weddings. Every / wedding.
column2: Lloro en las bodas. En / todas.

column1: I wanted to be a painter.
I still sleep with the light / on.
column2: Aún duermo con la luz / prendida.

column1: I'm not as happy as I look.
column2: No soy tan feliz como parezco.

column1: I miss my mum's cooking.
I talk to my plants. They / talk back. Quietly.
column2: Hablo con mis plantas. Me / responden. Bajito.

column1: I never said sorry to my / best friend.
column2: Nunca le pedí perdón a mi / mejor amigo.

column1: I'm scared of being boring.
I don't like parties. I come / anyway.
column2: No me gustan las fiestas. Voy / igual.

column1: I'm lonely on Sundays.
I'm afraid of getting old.
I pretend to read the news.
I wanted to go over there. / My whole life.
column2: Quería ir allá. Toda mi / vida.

column1: I failed my driving test six / times.
column2: Reprobé el examen de manejo / seis veces.

column1: I hate my laugh.
I'm scared of the Wall. Even / now it's coming down.
column2: Le temo al Muro. Aun ahora / que se derrumba.

column1: I lied about my age.
I don't know what I want.
I'm jealous of my sister.
I worry nobody will come to / my funeral.
column2: Temo que nadie vaya a mi / funeral.

column1: I eat the last cookie. Every / time. It's me.
column2: Me como la última galleta. / Siempre. Soy yo.

column1: I'm sorry I left.
I never told her I loved her.
column2: Nunca le dije que la amaba.

column1: I'm afraid of thunder.
I can't sing. I sing anyway.
I don't like my job.
I miss the old park.
I think about the other side / every day.
column2: Pienso en el otro lado / cada día.

column1: I'm scared I'm not a good / parent.
I have no idea what I'm / doing. Ever.
column2: No tengo idea de lo que / hago. Nunca.

column1: I hid in the bathroom at my / own birthday.
column2: Me escondí en el baño en mi / propio cumpleaños.

column1: I never forgave myself.
I want to start again.
I'm scared of the fountain.
I was a little bit possessed / once. It was nice. Sorry.
column2: Estuve un poquito poseído / una vez. Fue lindo. Perdón.

column1: I don't actually like / cupcakes.
column2: En realidad no me gustan / los cupcakes.

column1: I write letters I never send.
I'm afraid I'll be forgotten.
I keep my dad's hat. It / still smells like him.
column2: Guardo el sombrero de mi / papá. Aún huele a él.

column1: I'm happy. Really happy. / Today. It scares me.
column2: Soy feliz. Muy feliz. / Hoy. Me da miedo.

column1: I kept a soot sprite in a / jar. I let it go today.
column2: Guardé un duendecillo de / hollín en un frasco. Hoy lo solté.

column1: I thought I was the only / one.
I'm older than I tell you. / I'm tired. I bake anyway.
column2: Soy mayor de lo que digo. / Estoy cansada. Horneo igual.

column1: I cried. A lot. That's okay, / right? It's okay.
column2: Lloré. Mucho. Está bien, / ¿verdad? Está bien.

column1: I don't always know if it / works. I hug anyway.
column2: No siempre sé si funciona. / Abrazo igual.

column1: I missed home. Every / single day.
column2: Extrañé mi hogar. Todos / los días.

column1: I'm from here.
I get lonely in the steam.
I'm funny so nobody looks / too close.
column2: Soy gracioso para que nadie / mire de cerca.

column1: I'm scared of forgetting / you. All of you.
Monsters are real. They / also nap.
column2: Los monstruos existen. Y / también duermen siesta.

column1: The cloud was the only one / who listened. I was wrong.
column2: La nube era la única que / escuchaba. Me equivoqué.

column1: I set his bowl every year.
I don't know what to do / with my hands.
column2: No sé qué hacer con las / manos.

column1: I wanted something to grow / where nothing grows.
column2: Quería algo que creciera / donde nada crece.

column1: I was afraid of air.
I thought she hated me.
i was scared i'd never wake / up.
I like the smell of rain.
column2: Me gusta el olor a lluvia.

column1: I name every ghost I cough. / I miss them.
column2: Nombro a cada fantasma que / toso. Los extraño.

column1: Three, then one. Still here.
Nobody ever came up to / see my gate.
column2: Nadie vino a ver mi portón.

column1: I'm not a bother.
I'm scared of clowns.
The glitter isn't fine. / {..}It's mostly fine.
column2: El brillo no está bien. / {..}Está casi bien.

column1: I read every letter.
My poems are about her.
I hate paperwork.
I never wanted the foghorn.
column2: Nunca quise la sirena de niebla.

column1: I'm never in the photos.
The cookies were burnt on / purpose. So she'd write.
column2: Quemé las galletas a / propósito. Para que escribiera.

column1: Meet Nox? On the OTHER side? Me? Properly? In the daylight?
column2: ¿Conocer a Nox? ¿Al OTRO lado? ¿Yo? ¿De verdad? ¿A la luz del día?

column1: ...You walked through demons for us. I can walk through a gate.
column2: ...Cruzaste demonios por nosotros. Yo puedo cruzar un portón.

column1: I'll bring cupcakes. Nana / made them. Everyone likes / cupcakes.
column2: Llevaré cupcakes. Los hizo / Nana. A todos les gustan / los cupcakes.

column1: (His hands shake on the gate handle. Rivet's bead is still warm.)
column2: (Le tiemblan las manos en la manija del portón. La cuenta de Rivet aún está tibia.)

column1: Mayor. Love the hat.
It's my head.
{d}I know.
Mum. The fountain. Two-way, / like you made it.
column2: Mamá. La fuente. En ambos / sentidos, como la hiciste.

column1: You're my hands. I'll call / the rhythm. Ready?
column2: Tú eres mis manos. Yo marco / el ritmo. ¿Lista?

column1: Your turn. What did you / never say?
I was lonely.
I was scared too.
I like it here.
I'm home.
(Mascotty walks into the / rubble. She takes off her / head. For the first time.)
column2: (Mascotty entra a los / escombros. Se quita la / cabeza. Por primera vez.)

column1: (A small, tired bunnykin.)
(Thumpkin thumps the ground / once.)
(She thumps back. Once.)
(They hug.)
Two kids on a blanket at the / Mingle, forty years ago.
column2: Dos niños en una manta en el / Mingle, hace cuarenta años.

column1: LITTLE NOX: Soup's better.
column2: NOX NIÑA: La sopa es mejor.

column1: LITTLE GIGGS: ...Cupcakes / are better.
BOTH: ...Both are better.
(Two tables pushed together. Two bowls. A plate of cupcakes.)
column2: (Dos mesas juntas. Dos platos. Una bandeja de cupcakes.)

column1: MAYOR: Nox. {..}I brought / cupcakes.
NOX: {d}...I brought bone / soup.
MAYOR: ...I LOVE soup.
NOX: You're late.
MAYOR: I closed it.
NOX: I let you.
(Vex sets the jar on the / table. A grey cloud, the / size of a cupcake.)
column2: (Vex pone el frasco en la / mesa. Una nube gris del / tamaño de un cupcake.)

column1: MAYOR: ...Hi, Fluffy.
(Two drops of rain, inside / the jar.)
column2: (Dos gotas de lluvia dentro / del frasco.)

column1: VAPULA: (drip.)
VAPULA: (drip.) (drip.)
MAYOR: Hee. Hee.
MAYOR: I was scared. I'm / still scared.{..} Hold my / hand?
column2: ALCALDE: Tenía miedo. Aún / tengo.{..} ¿Me tomas la / mano?

column1: (She takes it.)
NOX: Then I believe we have / nothing left to build a / Wall for.
column2: NOX: Entonces creo que ya no / queda nada para lo que / construir un Muro.

column1: (The jar stays dry.)
MAYOR: ...hi, Fluffy.
(Everyone walks to the Wall. / Both sides.)
column2: (Todos caminan hasta el Muro. / De ambos lados.)

column1: (Rivet and Anvil re-plumb the fountain. Two-way. A new hammer mark.)
column2: (Rivet y Anvil reinstalan la fuente. En ambos sentidos. Una nueva marca de martillo.)

column1: (The giggle bubbles stack / against the Wall. It's your / turn.)
column2: (Las burbujas de risa se / apilan contra el Muro. Es / tu turno.)
